Devon S.: Heads up — ran a KMS provider failover test in staging at 09:12 and noticed some snapshot immutability flags on older backups were missing after the failover.
Ari: wait, "immutability flags" meaning object lock / retention metadata got stripped?
Devon S.: Exactly. S3 object metadata retained X-Amz-Object-Lock-Mode/RetainUntilDate removed for ~8 snapshots.
Mike L.: any error in uploader logs during the window?
Devon S.: Logs show successful upload, then a provider switch step — uploader retried with a different KMS endpoint. No explicit error.
encops-bot: alert: kms-provider-failover detected for project:tenant-42 at 2026-03-20T09:13:02Z — 1.2m duration
Devon S.: engineer steps so far:
- checked uploader serviceaccount IAM (no perms changes)
- queried audit logs for kms:Encrypt/Decrypt calls
- verified object headers after the fact
Ari: can you paste the audit query and results? makes it easier to triage.
Devon S.: query:
```
SELECT timestamp, actor, action, resource_name, request_params
FROM audit_logs
WHERE resource_type = 'kms_key' AND timestamp >= '2026-03-20T09:00:00Z' AND timestamp <= '2026-03-20T09:20:00Z';
```
results: two provider switch grants, one decrypt call that returned 403 for uploader, then a successful decrypt by a fallback service.
Security Oncall: 403 during decrypt is the red flag — who had temporary grants? that smells like an ephemeral grant expiration or wrong key alias mapping.
Mike L.: uploader should fail closed if decrypt fails; but if fallback service later rewrites metadata, that could cause the missing immutability headers.
Ari: do we have a replay of object write flows? need S3 PUT events and corresponding metadata writes.
Devon S.: pulled these:
```
PUT /snapshots/tenant-42/2026-03-20T09:12:05Z size=2.1GB metadata:{object-lock-mode=GOVERNANCE, retain-until=2028-03-20T09:12:05Z}
PUT /snapshots/tenant-42/2026-03-20T09:14:12Z size=2.1GB metadata:{object-lock-mode=, retain-until=}
```
Ari: that's the race — second PUT overwrote headers. which service created second PUT?
Devon S.: fallback-uploader (service) did it. It was triggered after a decrypt 403 and attempted recovery.
Security Oncall: action items:
- revert fallback-uploader's auto-rewrite behavior for snapshot PUTs (block until manual review)
- add a strict RBAC check to prevent fallback-uploader from changing object-lock headers
- emit an alert if a PUT occurs that removes object-lock metadata
Mike L.: Agree. Also add an audit log detector rule: if object-lock headers present at first PUT and absent on subsequent PUT for same key within 24h, trigger triage.
Devon S.: I'll open a ticket and draft runbook changes. Draft steps in the runbook:
1) Detect affected keys and isolate (list of object keys attached)
2) Move impacted snapshots to quarantined bucket with original metadata preserved
3) Run restore test from quarantined copies
4) Revoke fallback-uploader write permissions until a patch
5) Notify affected tenants + legal if retention policies may be violated
Ari: for KMS integration: we need to ensure key alias resolution is atomic during provider failover. If alias resolution returns a different key or temporary 403, uploader must not fallback to another service that re-encrypts with a different key silently.
Devon S.: Proposed quick fixes:
- uploader: on decrypt 403, retry with exponential backoff x3, then fail and emit high-sev alert
- fallback-uploader: drop privilege to only upload to staging/quarantine unless explicit OK
- enforce server-side encryption headers immutability via object-store policy
Security Oncall: also add a scheduled test: monthly simulated KMS endpoint rotation test with end-to-end invariant checks for immutability and audit logs.
encops-bot: runbook update created: RBAC-4367 — https://redwood-internal/ops/RBAC-4367
Mike L.: will add unit/integration tests to uploader and fallback-uploader. Also will add a preflight mutex when writing metadata to avoid two services racing.
Devon S.: FYI I'm running a scan now to list all snapshots that had header removal between 2026-03-20T09:00 and 2026-03-20T10:00, will paste results here when done.
Ari: Also let's consider adding kms:GrantCreate permission auditing and require short-lived grants be logged with a correlation ID passed in the S3 metadata.
Security Oncall: good idea. correlation ID will help trace which actor triggered the fallback rewrite.
Devon S.: (later) scan results: 8 affected snapshot keys, 5 tenants impacted. Moving to quarantine now.
Mike L.: thanks — assigning me to RBAC-4367 to implement the uploader changes.
Ari: I'll draft the audit alert and update the compliance runbook section on retention contract breaches.
Devon S.: thanks all. pairing on patch review tomorrow 10:00. :thumbsup:
encops-bot: ticket RBAC-4367 updated: state=In Progress, assignee=Mike L.
Security Oncall: closing the loop: we'll keep this as postmortem-lite in next sec retro.
